input.rationale: A Vendor IP infringement indemnity is present. Section 13 (continuing at p0090) has Garman represent and warrant that it owns or controls all rights necessary to grant the licence and that no lien, encumbrance or third-party right will interfere with Sparkling's rights, and then provides that "Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless" from all Losses — expressly including amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and investigation costs — arising from breach of that warranty. The same paragraph deals directly with the infringement scenario ("If the Work or any portion thereof is held to constitute an infringement of another Person's rights, and use thereof is enjoined"), obliging Garman at its own expense to procure the right to use the infringing element, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify the Work so it is non-infringing without material loss of functionality (p0091–p0093). That is a Vendor IP indemnity with the usual remedy ladder, i.e. the rule's fallback position. Direction is correct: the indemnity runs from Garman to us, and there is no reverse or one-way Sparkling indemnity for Garman's software or services anywhere in the agreement, so the walk-away case does not arise. Section 15 is also better than the fallback: the cap and the consequential/indirect damages exclusion "shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14", leaving the IP indemnity uncapped rather than subject to a 3x super-cap. Recorded as internal evidence only, short of the preferred position and not flagged as deviations: no express "defend"/control-of-defence and cooperation mechanic, no refund remedy if none of (a)-(c) can be achieved, indemnity limited to IP/title matters (no breach-of-law, Customer Data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs), affiliates not named as beneficiaries, and a tight ten-calendar-day notice obligation on us. Compliant at the fallback; no redline proposed.
